summary:
CropCast is an Arabic-first web platform that turns NASA Earth observation data into a simple, evidence-based “case file” for farmers and investors. A farmer pins their field by GPS, uploads a land photo and enters what they know. CropCast compares current rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation conditions with past seasons, explains the results in plain language, and compares crop-rotation scenarios according to the farmer’s priority: water saving, soil health or season risk. Every finding states what we observed, the evidence, what we don’t know, and where local expertise is needed. Strong land can be listed for investors, who receive an investment-focused risk report and timeline.

CropCast addresses the Field Shift challenge by linking climate and soil indicators to crop stress and rotation choices, while being open about uncertainty. It matters because farmers face climate stress and small, fragmented holdings, investors lack trusted information about land, and free NASA data rarely reaches them in a usable form.
details:
What it does and how it works
CropCast is an Arabic-first web platform for farmers and investors. It turns NASA Earth observation data and local inputs into a plain-language “case file” about a piece of land.

  • The farmer pins the field by GPS, uploads a land photo and enters what they know (crop, area, irrigation, soil, priority).
  • The system compares rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation (NDVI) with past seasons using z-score and percentile rank, then explains the results and the uncertainty.
  • It compares crop-rotation scenarios by the farmer’s priority (water saving, soil health, season risk).
  • Weak land gets AI improvement guidance. Strong land can be listed for investors, with the farmer’s consent.
  • Investors get matched land with a risk report and timeline, and an admin panel flags suspicious data for review.
    Benefits
  • Farmers get simple, evidence-based insight and rotation options matched to their priorities.
  • Investors get trusted, data-backed information about land.
  • Uncertainty is stated openly, so the tool supports local expertise instead of replacing it
    Impact
  • Support adaptation to climate stress and better soil and water management
  • Connect productive land to investment and contribute to food security
    Tools and technologies
  • NASA data: GPM IMERG (rainfall), SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS/Landsat NDVI (vegetation)
  • Programming languages: TypeScript and JavaScript (React), HTML/CSS (Tailwind CSS) ,Python
  • Hardware: none special. It runs in a laptop or phone browser, using the phone’s GPS and camera
    What makes it creative
  • It offers an “evidence-based consultation, not a magic answer”: each finding states what we observed, the evidence, what we don’t know and the next step
  • It reports data sufficiency instead of a fake confidence score
  • One platform serves both sides, farmers and investors, with AI checking submitted data for authenticity
  • It was designed with simple Arabic, optional inputs, no guessing for missing information
    Factors the team considered
  • Scientific honesty: each NASA layer is shown at its native resolution, with no upscaling presented as field-level measurement
  • Uncertainty and local expertise: the tool flags where an agronomist should verify results
  • Simplicity: limited technical background, so plain language and optional inputs
  • Trust and privacy: land is shared with investors only with the farmer’s consent, and AI flags suspicious data while a human admin decides
  • Feasibility: a focused prototype and a pilot area, with expansion planned later
projectRefs: LAND at scale study (Egypt land fragmentation)
